body: Six categories (slow growers, stalwarts, fast growers, cyclicals, turnarounds, asset plays); PEG ~1; know the story. Real edge: 200+ company visits & ~700 annual reports/yr, ~300% turnover, up to 1,400 stocks; pre-Reg FD access. 'Buy what you know' is a starting point only.
title: Peter Lynch: categories, PEG, relentless research

body: Principles from Margin of Safety (1991) and Baupost letters: (1) Value conservatively (liquidation, private-market or cash-flow value) and buy only at a large discount - the discount is the protection against your own errors. (2) Think about downside first; absolute, not relative, returns. (3) Look where selling is non-economic: forced or constrained sellers (index deletions, spin-offs, bankruptcy, fund redemptions, regulatory rules) and complex/illiquid securities. (4) Catalysts (asset sales, buybacks, restructuring) shorten the wait. (5) Hold cash when nothing qualifies - cash is a call option on future bargains. Indian forced-seller situations: MF scheme recategorisation (2017-18), index exits, promoter pledge invocations, ASM/GSM-listed stocks after rule-driven selling, demerged entities on listing, rights-issue discounts. Evidence: Baupost's strong first 25 years and weak post-2014 decade show the method depends on the opportunity set - it shines after crashes and lags in long, liquidity-driven bulls.
title: Klarman: margin of safety, forced sellers, and cash as an option
